input: Run each of the four old revisions and one source path plus the scope control exactly as frozen in final_synthesis_repr_v2_selection_pre.json. Read only that old C file and at most three edges of quoted local includes. Do not provide the fix revision to the scanner.
predeclared_classification: candidate means a local source review lead: proven host-typed value to __le/__be field or a native-width aliased byte slot beside same-order endian fields, with pointer-parameter or same-function call evidence. It does not prove hardware consumption, the authoritative byte order, or a defect.
normal is valid only for the analyzed site when a same-representation value, proven host-value conversion, or zero is present. A local normal never clears the function or commit.

insufficient covers unknown RHS type, unproven conversion, ambiguous declaration, missing caller boundary, and unsupported syntax. Zero recognized sites means out of checker scope, not a clean commit.
Runner error or unavailable source is separate from all three outcomes. No target will be replaced based on raw output or later source review.
normal_controls: Before target review, offline synthetic tests cover correct cpu_to_le/be conversion, same-representation copy, and zero; old/fixed development playback provides real old-version local normal sites. In new targets, report any local normal sites individually and do not infer whole-file correctness. The fifth title-selected input is a scope control, not a presumed normal control.
review_order: Run the frozen checker on all five old revisions and save raw JSON plus SHA-256 hashes before opening any selected target source or fix body/diff.

Then inspect exact old-source and fix-patch mechanisms, candidate line correspondence, supported configuration, source of representation authority, and whether each output is useful, a miss, or a justified refusal.
Count independent causal chains by commit after review, not assignment count. Report purposefully selected unseen-source cases without population accuracy, precision, recall, or speed claims.
stop_rule: Do not mutate checker/test/protocol or replace selected targets after seeing outputs. Any next detector revision requires a fresh, separately frozen target set.
